groups.title: OAuth flow and session management in NextAuth
groups.question: Users sign in to your T3 app with GitHub, and you must decide how sessions are stored. Explain how the login flow works and the trade-offs between session types.

followUps.How OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow wo: Walk through what happens between clicking 'Sign in with GitHub' and being logged in.
followUps.JWT strategy versus database sessions: t: Why can't you instantly log out a user with JWT sessions, and what does a database session cost?

evidence.text: The user is sent to GitHub to log in and approve access.
GitHub redirects back to the app with a short-lived authorization code.
The server exchanges that code for tokens and the user's profile, then creates a session.

notEnough: Only saying OAuth lets users log in with another account.

misconceptions.text: Says the app receives the user's GitHub password.

evidence.text: JWT sessions are stored in the token itself, so no database lookup is needed.
A JWT stays valid until it expires, so it cannot be revoked instantly.
Database sessions can be revoked at once but need a database query on each request.

notEnough: Only saying one uses tokens and one uses a database.

groups.title: Protecting tRPC procedures and Next.js routes
groups.question: Some pages and tRPC procedures must only be used by signed-in users, and some only by admins. Explain how you would read the session on the server and enforce roles.

followUps.Reading the session in server components: How do you get the session in a server component or tRPC context?
followUps.Role-based authorization in protected tR: How would you add a role to the session and use it to block non-admins?

evidence.text: A server-side helper reads the session from the request cookies.
This happens on the server without an extra HTTP request.
It is used in tRPC context creation and in server components and layouts.
The session type is extended to include the user's role.
Middleware on admin procedures checks the role.
Users without the right role get a forbidden error, separate from being unauthenticated.

notEnough: Only saying you check if the user is admin.

groups.title: Configuring NextAuth in a T3 app
groups.question: You are setting up authentication in a fresh T3 app with GitHub and Google login, storing users in your database. Explain the setup and where secrets go.

followUps.Setting up the Prisma adapter for user a: What does the Prisma adapter do for NextAuth?
followUps.Configuring GitHub and Google OAuth prov: Where do the GitHub client ID and secret come from, and where must they be stored?

evidence.text: The adapter stores users, accounts, sessions and verification tokens in your database.
Those models are added to the Prisma schema and created with a migration.
It links each sign-in provider account to a single user record.

notEnough: Only saying it connects NextAuth to Prisma.

evidence.text: You register an OAuth app with GitHub or Google to get a client ID and secret.
The provider must know your app's callback URL to send users back.
The secret is stored in environment variables and never in code or the client bundle.

notEnough: Only saying you add providers to the config.

groups.title: Client-side session access and sign-in/out
groups.question: Your navbar shows the user's avatar, and you need sign-in and sign-out buttons that send users to the right page. Explain how client components access and change the session.

followUps.useSession hook for accessing session in: What does useSession return, and what is needed for it to work?
followUps.signIn and signOut functions and redirec: How do signIn and signOut decide where the user ends up?

evidence.text: The app must be wrapped in a SessionProvider for useSession to work.
useSession returns the session and a status of loading, authenticated or unauthenticated.
The UI should handle the loading status instead of assuming the user is signed out.

notEnough: Only saying it returns the session.

evidence.text: signIn starts the login flow for a provider.
A callback URL sets where the user is redirected after signing in or out.
signOut clears the session cookie before redirecting.

notEnough: Only saying they log the user in and out.
